(loss functions, optimizers) is required before using a framework like PyTorch."}],"phases":[{"id":"a41118c1-baa3-465f-8757-84b2593e5386","title":"Phase 1: Foundational Mathematics and Scientific Python","description":"This phase establishes the critical mathematical and programming prerequisites. You will solidify your Python skills for numerical computing and learn the core linear algebra, calculus, and probability concepts that form the language of machine learning and neural networks, with no prior knowledge assumed.","order":1,"chapters":[{"id":"fcbf8c63-cbfd-4493-8b15-058428930624","title":"Python Programming Fundamentals for Scientific Computing","description":"Reinforces core Python syntax and constructs with a focus on numerical and data tasks. Covers essential data structures (lists, dictionaries, tuples), control flow, functions, and basic file I/O. Emphasizes writing clean, reproducible code and setting up a virtual environment for project management.","order":1},{"id":"9c6f9d31-b036-4e70-b014-826d92fdf7cb","title":"Numerical Computing and Array Operations with NumPy","description":"Introduces NumPy as the foundational library for efficient numerical computation. Covers creating, indexing, and manipulating multi-dimensional arrays (ndarrays), performing vectorized operations, understanding broadcasting rules, and applying essential mathematical and linear algebra functions.","order":2},{"id":"f1bf7e9b-c5dd-470e-9b06-3f95c6f5f86d","title":"Linear Algebra Concepts Applied with NumPy","description":"Presents core linear algebra principles through the lens of NumPy operations. Focuses on vectors, matrices, and tensors as data structures; key operations (dot products, matrix multiplication, transposition); and foundational concepts including norms, eigenvalues/vectors, and singular value decomposition (SVD) for practical application.","order":3},{"id":"b4ef56b2-afb8-4c03-af48-65cdcd4fef02","title":"Calculus Fundamentals: Derivatives, Gradients, and Optimization","description":"Introduces the differential calculus required to understand model training dynamics. Explores functions, derivatives, partial derivatives, and the gradient vector. Focuses on the conceptual interpretation of the derivative as an instantaneous rate of change and the gradient as pointing toward the steepest ascent, establishing the basis for gradient-based optimization.","order":4},{"id":"c1e18cf2-4a5b-4127-978a-7dc95e1c4609","title":"Probability Theory and Statistical Measures for Machine Learning","description":"Covers the probabilistic and statistical reasoning essential for ML. Includes fundamental probability rules, key discrete and continuous distributions (e.g., Bernoulli, Normal), descriptive statistics (mean, variance, covariance), and introduces maximum likelihood estimation and Bayes' Theorem at a conceptual level.","order":5},{"id":"8102a39d-5487-4eaa-acdf-118cc50ff477","title":"Data Wrangling and Manipulation with Pandas","description":"Introduces structured data manipulation using Pandas. Focuses on the core data structures (Series and DataFrame) for data ingestion, cleaning, filtering, grouping, and aggregation. Establishes Pandas as the primary tool for preparing tabular datasets for analysis and modeling.","order":6},{"id":"cd433acd-db08-4367-a941-dcceff261496","title":"Data Visualization and Exploration with Matplotlib & Seaborn","description":"Covers the principles of creating effective visualizations for data exploration. Uses Matplotlib to build foundational plots (line plots, scatter plots, histograms) and introduces Seaborn for more advanced statistical graphics. Teaches how to visualize distributions, relationships, and patterns to generate insights.","order":7},{"id":"b210a01c-a4b2-427a-bf5f-4516ebfa833d","title":"Integrated Capstone Project: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)","description":"A comprehensive project applying all phase skills. Students perform a complete EDA on a classic dataset (e.g., Iris, Boston Housing). Tasks include data loading and cleaning with Pandas, numerical analysis with NumPy, statistical summarization, and creating a visual narrative with Matplotlib/Seaborn to uncover key patterns, relationships, and hypotheses.","order":8}]},{"id":"5d2150c9-fee5-4868-bc9b-16aa00bf0c38","title":"Phase 2: Introduction to Machine Learning Concepts","description":"This phase introduces the fundamental paradigms and workflow of machine learning. You will learn core concepts like supervised vs. unsupervised learning, model training, validation, testing, overfitting, and basic algorithms (e.g., linear regression) to build intuition before diving into deep learning.","order":2,"chapters":[{"id":"7eedf760-778c-428b-b73c-a76d2e964ffe","title":"The Machine Learning Landscape","description":"This chapter introduces the core paradigms of machine learning. You will learn the definitions and key differences between supervised learning (for labeled prediction), unsupervised learning (for discovering hidden structure), and reinforcement learning (for sequential decision-making). The chapter establishes the fundamental concept of a model as a function learned from data, illustrated with real-world examples for each paradigm.","order":1},{"id":"f938a71e-63da-4a0d-a4aa-6af2f851bcc3","title":"The Model Development Workflow","description":"This chapter details the standardized, iterative process for building a machine learning model. You will learn the critical steps: problem formulation, data collection and preprocessing, splitting data into distinct training, validation, and test sets, model selection and training, and performance evaluation. This framework is essential for all subsequent practical work.","order":2},{"id":"6ae6a0d3-bb86-440c-a0c3-576bbe9985d4","title":"Evaluating Performance and Managing Generalization","description":"This chapter focuses on quantifying model success and diagnosing failure modes. You will learn key evaluation metrics for regression (Mean Squared Error, R-squared) and classification (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score). It introduces the core concepts of overfitting (memorizing noise) vs. underfitting (missing patterns), the bias-variance tradeoff, and the role of the validation set in model selection.","order":3},{"id":"10fb70f1-263f-4a2f-b5e0-87100e7c0e8c","title":"A First Supervised Model: Linear Regression","description":"This chapter applies core concepts by building a foundational algorithm from first principles. You will learn linear regression as a parametric model, defining its hypothesis and cost function (Mean Squared Error). The chapter covers the analytical ordinary least squares solution and introduces the concept of iterative optimization, setting the stage for gradient descent.","order":4},{"id":"506cafa6-bd1f-47cd-9f45-b2cf071cb40f","title":"From Regression to Classification: Logistic Regression","description":"This chapter extends the principles of linear models to classification tasks. You will learn the logistic function (sigmoid) for modeling probabilities, formulate the cross-entropy loss function, and understand how to interpret model outputs as class likelihoods. This bridges the gap between linear regression and more complex classifiers.","order":5},{"id":"d9ac0fae-0b05-49b8-82f3-28b39d42e4c6","title":"Learning Without Labels: Core Unsupervised Methods","description":"This chapter explores the objectives and algorithms for learning from unlabeled data. You will be introduced to clustering (grouping similar data points, exemplified by K-Means) and dimensionality reduction (simplifying data while preserving structure, exemplified by Principal Component Analysis). The chapter contrasts these goals with the supervised framework.","order":6}]},{"id":"e9a313bb-0ea4-41f0-8d48-ad5b05a011fb","title":"Phase 3: Fundamentals of Neural Networks","description":"This phase demystifies the core mechanics of neural networks. You will learn about neurons, layers, activation functions, the forward pass, loss functions, and the essential backpropagation algorithm for training, building them from scratch using NumPy to deeply understand the concepts.","order":3,"chapters":[{"id":"9c88cba1-636e-4e04-b5fe-79b90de7fb0d","title":"The Biological Analogy and the Mathematical Model of a Neuron","description":"This chapter establishes the conceptual bridge from biology to computation. You will learn how the core concepts of a biological neuron (inputs, synaptic weights, summation, threshold firing) inspired the creation of the perceptron. You will then define the formal mathematical model of an artificial neuron, including weights, the bias term, and the weighted sum.","order":1},{"id":"856db600-2e92-4775-8557-40eefb67e157","title":"Introducing Non-Linearity: Activation Functions","description":"This chapter explains the critical component that allows neural networks to model complex patterns. You will learn why linear activation is insufficient and explore the purpose, mathematical form, and derivative of essential activation functions (Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU), comparing their behavior, output ranges, and impact on gradient flow.","order":2},{"id":"d966d901-ec17-4d65-a43d-378d5bcd6cdd","title":"Architecting a Network: Layers and Topology","description":"This chapter explains how to build a computational graph from individual neurons. You will learn to define a network's architecture through layers (input, hidden, output), width, and depth. You will understand how layers are connected via weight matrices and bias vectors, forming the structure for the forward pass.","order":3},{"id":"721eff62-ae5b-42c6-9a09-f74d023373da","title":"Computing Predictions: The Forward Pass","description":"This chapter details the step-by-step computation to generate a prediction. You will learn to express the forward pass for a multi-layer network as sequential linear transformations (matrix multiplications + bias addition) followed by non-linear activation. You will implement this full process in NumPy, calculating pre-activations (Z) and activations (A) for all layers.","order":4},{"id":"65deb479-73cf-4373-8265-c64d015b8453","title":"Measuring Performance: Loss Functions","description":"This chapter covers how to quantify the discrepancy between predictions and reality. You will learn the purpose and properties of loss functions. You will derive, implement, and apply foundational examples: Mean Squared Error (MSE) for regression and Cross-Entropy Loss for classification.","order":5},{"id":"b8c161e7-ae8b-4e8d-ab93-b49fe9c7d029","title":"The Engine of Learning: Gradient Descent & Backpropagation Intuition","description":"This chapter introduces the core optimization principle and the high-level logic of the training algorithm. You will learn the concept of gradients and how Gradient Descent uses them to minimize loss. You will then understand the goal of backpropagation—to compute the gradient for every parameter efficiently—and trace the flow of error backward through a network conceptually using the chain rule.","order":6},{"id":"ad1b70f3-d86f-428e-8194-4b19d0ba0a81","title":"Calculating Gradients: The Math of Backpropagation","description":"This chapter provides the detailed mathematical derivation for parameter updates. You will compute the gradients of the loss with respect to weights and biases for a simple multi-layer network. You will derive the formulas step-by-step using the chain rule for a specific architecture (e.g., MSE loss with Sigmoid activation) and translate these equations into a structured NumPy implementation.","order":7},{"id":"e96d91b5-49b7-4bfb-a3ce-0b069c01985e","title":"The Complete Training Loop: From Initialization to Update","description":"This chapter integrates all components into a functioning learning algorithm. You will learn methods for initializing network parameters (e.g., small random values). You will then write a full NumPy training loop that iteratively performs a forward pass, computes the loss, executes backpropagation to obtain gradients, and updates all parameters using a simple Gradient Descent update rule.","order":8},{"id":"67549fd3-8c51-4198-b68e-c3c7e6655e12","title":"Capstone: Training and Evaluating Your First Network","description":"This final chapter applies the complete framework to a concrete problem. You will generate or load a simple synthetic dataset (like the XOR problem). You will then train a small neural network from scratch using your code, monitor the loss during training, and finally evaluate the trained model's performance on held-out data, observing its learned decision boundaries.","order":9}]},{"id":"a91e37e4-99ad-4b1f-948b-e9af6b70efc4","title":"Phase 4: PyTorch Core: Tensors, Autograd, and Basic Models","description":"This phase is your first hands-on experience with PyTorch. You will learn its core data structure (Tensors), perform operations, and harness the automatic differentiation engine (Autograd) to efficiently compute gradients. You will then rebuild the basic neural networks from the previous phase using PyTorch's built-in components.","order":4,"chapters":[{"id":"372b180b-21a2-4c70-8976-76e34521d041","title":"Introduction to PyTorch and its Computational Philosophy","description":"This chapter introduces PyTorch, its ecosystem, and core philosophy. You will contrast its dynamic \"define-by-run\" approach with static graph frameworks, set up a PyTorch environment (including GPU verification), and explore the structure of the `torch` library and its seamless integration with Python and NumPy.","order":1},{"id":"9a30ddac-6f45-4d12-9d8a-9a90a9aaeea6","title":"The Tensor: PyTorch's Fundamental Data Structure","description":"This chapter covers the foundational Tensor object. You will learn to create tensors from various sources (lists, NumPy), inspect and manipulate their key properties (`shape`, `dtype`, `device`), and perform essential data manipulations like reshaping, slicing, and concatenation. You will also learn to move tensors between CPU and GPU memory.","order":2},{"id":"79c10c9d-f258-4d26-a8dc-e7baf9565981","title":"Tensor Operations, Broadcasting, and Initialization","description":"This chapter focuses on computations with tensors. You will perform element-wise and matrix operations, use reduction functions (e.g., `sum`, `mean`), and apply PyTorch's broadcasting rules for efficient code. You will also learn standard methods for initializing tensors (e.g., random, zeros), which are critical for setting model parameters.","order":3},{"id":"4b79099b-134d-458a-b1b8-e1323a6b68dd","title":"Automatic Differentiation with Autograd","description":"This chapter explains PyTorch's automatic differentiation engine. You will learn how tensors build a dynamic computational graph via `.requires_grad`, compute gradients with `.backward()`, and access derivatives via the `.grad` attribute. You will also learn to control gradient tracking using `torch.no_grad()` and `.detach()` for efficient evaluation and inference.","order":4},{"id":"4215b259-34c2-4218-a111-e9b51cfc8d33","title":"Neural Network Building Blocks: `nn.Module` and `nn.Parameter`","description":"This chapter introduces the high-level `torch.nn` API. You will learn to define custom network components by subclassing `nn.Module`, register trainable parameters with `nn.Parameter`, and use pre-defined layers like `nn.Linear`. The chapter covers the module lifecycle: initialization, the `forward()` method, and sub-module management.","order":5},{"id":"62685301-28ea-4dcb-9f4c-206156005082","title":"From Theory to Code: Implementing Linear Regression","description":"This chapter applies core concepts to rebuild linear regression. You will define a custom `LinearRegression` module, manually compute the mean squared error loss, write a training loop that uses `autograd` for gradients, and perform parameter updates with basic gradient descent, solidifying the link between theory and PyTorch implementation.","order":6},{"id":"ec769141-32cd-4b9a-a4c9-e843c58401b8","title":"Building a Multi-Layer Perceptron with PyTorch's Full Toolkit","description":"This chapter scales up to construct a basic feedforward neural network using PyTorch's standard components. You will build an MLP using `nn.Sequential` and custom modules, incorporate activation functions (`nn.ReLU`), use built-in loss functions (`nn.MSELoss`), and train the model using an optimizer from `torch.optim` (e.g., `optim.SGD`).","order":7},{"id":"22add941-997d-4925-8cb9-a1821c0084e4","title":"Capstone Project: A Complete Training Pipeline","description":"This final chapter integrates all skills into an end-to-end workflow. You will load a simple dataset (e.g., Iris), preprocess it into tensors, define a model, select a loss and optimizer, write a full training loop with gradient zeroing, and evaluate the final model on a test set, establishing the standard pattern for future PyTorch projects.","order":8}]},{"id":"3b14de34-b391-4745-8d4c-ada33a9cb02d","title":"Phase 5: Building and Training Deep Learning Pipelines in PyTorch","description":"This phase focuses on the practical workflow of building, training, and evaluating deep learning models. You will learn to structure projects using `nn.Module`, create custom datasets and dataloaders, write training loops, use optimizers and schedulers, and implement proper validation and testing protocols.","order":5,"chapters":[{"id":"08e24107-06d8-4b18-a0ca-9d892fff4135","title":"Architecting Models with `nn.Module`","description":"Learn to structure all neural network components using PyTorch's foundational `nn.Module` class. This chapter covers defining layers in `__init__`, implementing the `forward` pass, creating modular sub-modules for complex architectures, and understanding the model's parameter management. You'll build custom, reusable model classes from the ground up.","order":1},{"id":"12b9297d-2392-4eea-8659-9fe9c32ca473","title":"Data Pipeline Engineering: Datasets and DataLoaders","description":"Master the process of feeding data to your models efficiently. Learn to use built-in PyTorch Dataset classes (e.g., `TensorDataset`, `ImageFolder`) and, crucially, how to write custom `Dataset` classes for your own data. Integrate these with the `DataLoader` for automatic batching, shuffling, and parallel data loading, forming the essential input pipeline.","order":2},{"id":"0874ad78-8af0-4c30-a23c-7a927e0906a7","title":"The Core Training Loop: Forward Pass, Loss, and Backward Pass","description":"Construct the fundamental training iteration. You will learn to write the step-by-step loop that executes the model forward pass, calculates the loss using functions from the `nn` module, performs the backward pass via `loss.backward()` to compute gradients, and applies an optimizer step to update parameters. This chapter establishes the basic mechanics of model learning.","order":3},{"id":"286c96c3-1981-4887-a08d-80572823d83b","title":"Configuring Optimization: Optimizers and Learning Rate Schedulers","description":"Control how your model learns by configuring the optimization process. Select and instantiate optimizers (like SGD and Adam), setting their key hyperparameters. Learn to dynamically adjust the learning rate during training using schedulers (e.g., StepLR, ReduceLROnPlateau) to improve convergence and final model performance.","order":4},{"id":"8b5738c7-fb07-435b-87d9-535b09270d7c","title":"Implementing Validation, Testing, and Model Checkpointing","description":"Move beyond training to rigorously evaluate and save your models. Implement separate validation and test loops to monitor metrics like accuracy and loss, using them to detect overfitting and report final performance. Learn to save and load the complete state of your model and optimizer using checkpointing, enabling you to resume training and deploy the best model.","order":5},{"id":"ffcd8e6c-1c72-45fe-a704-ae719269a874","title":"Monitoring, Debugging, and Visualization","description":"Learn to instrument and diagnose your training pipeline. Implement logging for key metrics. Use tools like TensorBoard or Weights & Biases to visualize loss curves, model graphs, and histograms of weights/gradients. Apply practical debugging techniques to identify and fix common issues like vanishing gradients or poor initialization.","order":6}]},{"id":"63bee2c9-d1f4-428b-9173-953608cc7968","title":"Phase 6: Core Neural Network Architectures: CNNs and RNNs","description":"This phase explores the two foundational architectures for structured data. You will learn Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image data and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs) for sequence data, understanding their layers, design principles, and how to implement them in PyTorch for tasks like image classification and time-series prediction.","order":6,"chapters":[{"id":"a18031e3-5901-4477-a5ec-50eaa189ff87","title":"The Need for CNNs: From Fully-Connected to Spatial Hierarchies","description":"This chapter establishes why Convolutional Neural Networks are essential for image data. You will learn the limitations of dense networks for high-dimensional inputs, the concept of parameter sharing and spatial invariance, and the core idea of learning hierarchical features (edges, textures, objects) from pixels.","order":1},{"id":"17f8b475-b795-435f-b112-973bd439305b","title":"The Convolution Operation: Kernels, Strides, and Padding","description":"This chapter delves into the mathematical and practical details of the convolution operation. You will learn how filters (kernels) slide across input data to produce feature maps, and master the hyperparameters that control this process: kernel size, stride, and padding. You will implement 2D convolution from scratch in NumPy to solidify understanding.","order":2},{"id":"c19fa62e-e375-453b-b7aa-c34971ac1e87","title":"Core CNN Building Blocks: Convolution, Pooling, and Activation Layers","description":"This chapter introduces the standard layers that form a CNN. You will learn the purpose and implementation of convolutional layers, various pooling operations (Max, Average), and non-linear activation functions (ReLU) within the CNN context. The chapter concludes by stacking these blocks to form a simple, complete CNN architecture diagram.","order":3},{"id":"10612524-3f19-4a14-bf31-c38c765958e0","title":"Implementing Your First CNN in PyTorch with `torch.nn`","description":"This chapter is your hands-on introduction to building CNNs using PyTorch's `nn` module. You will learn to use `nn.Conv2d`, `nn.MaxPool2d`, and `nn.Sequential` to construct a network (like LeNet) for the MNIST dataset. You will define the forward pass and understand the shape transformations through each layer.","order":4},{"id":"91e34ca9-47cd-48cf-a879-c3271610611a","title":"CNN Application: Image Classification Project","description":"This chapter consolidates CNN knowledge through a practical project. You will build a more powerful CNN (e.g., a small VGG-style net) to classify images from the CIFAR-10 dataset. You will implement data loading, training, validation, and analysis of results, while exploring the impact of depth and filter sizes.","order":5},{"id":"4296efd9-e4af-4df4-a9d9-bf2b47607f62","title":"Introduction to Sequence Modeling and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)","description":"This chapter transitions to sequential data like time-series or text. You will learn the concept of maintaining a hidden state, the structure of a basic RNN cell, and the unrolled computational graph. The chapter covers the challenges of processing sequences of variable length and the idea of many-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many architectures.","order":6},{"id":"90d6a04a-b673-47b0-a552-0db9101d740e","title":"Advanced RNN Architectures: LSTMs and GRUs","description":"This chapter addresses the fundamental limitations of vanilla RNNs: the vanishing/exploding gradient problem. You will learn in detail the gated mechanisms of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) units (input, forget, output gates, cell state) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs). You will understand how these gates enable the selective retention and forgetting of long-term information.","order":7},{"id":"38ba8e4b-c84b-4a62-aa9d-ff52d7474c10","title":"Implementing RNNs, LSTMs, and GRUs in PyTorch","description":"This chapter focuses on the practical implementation of sequence models in PyTorch. You will learn to use `nn.RNN`, `nn.LSTM`, and `nn.GRU` layers, manage input/output shapes for batches of sequences, and handle variable-length sequences using `torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence`. You will build a simple network for sentiment classification or next-character prediction.","order":8},{"id":"c0cf7431-8b31-44e4-b8ba-438aa081823e","title":"RNN Application: Time-Series Forecasting Project","description":"This chapter applies RNN knowledge to a classic sequence problem. You will build an LSTM model for time-series forecasting (e.g., predicting stock prices or weather data). You will learn to structure sequential data into windows, design appropriate many-to-one network architectures, and evaluate forecasting performance using metrics like Mean Squared Error.","order":9}]},{"id":"738f2bde-426c-4eb6-bc72-f8eb6ff7dce4","title":"Phase 7: Advanced Architectures and Modern Techniques","description":"This phase covers cutting-edge architectures and essential training techniques. You will study Transformer networks (the basis for LLMs), Autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and learn advanced methods like transfer learning, regularization techniques, and hyperparameter tuning to build robust, state-of-the-art models.","order":7,"chapters":[{"id":"9489e5b2-8725-45ac-a9e6-82b2bca1b1fa","title":"Systematic Hyperparameter Tuning and Advanced Model Evaluation","description":"Establish a rigorous engineering framework for model development. Learn automated hyperparameter optimization strategies (grid search, random search, Bayesian optimization with Optuna) and implement robust evaluation protocols. Move beyond basic accuracy to detailed error analysis, confusion matrices, and specialized metrics for generative models (e.g., FID, Inception Score).","order":1},{"id":"128f7e2e-07f4-42b7-be5d-7f04f13e9a06","title":"Advanced Optimization Algorithms and Training Dynamics","description":"Master the modern optimizer toolkit. Implement and contrast advanced algorithms (AdamW, RMSProp, AdaGrad), apply adaptive learning rate schedules (cyclic, cosine annealing, warm restarts), and utilize techniques like gradient clipping. Diagnose complex training issues by exploring concepts of loss landscapes, sharp vs. flat minima, and the dynamics of vanishing/exploding gradients.","order":2},{"id":"deaf886b-dac1-4949-b82a-e5ac4f6b9d9c","title":"Modern Regularization and Normalization Techniques","description":"Enhance model generalization and stability with advanced techniques. Implement and compare normalization layers (Batch, Layer, Instance, Group Normalization) and study architectural regularization methods (Stochastic Depth, DropBlock, CutMix). Understand the theoretical motivation behind each technique and its application in vision and sequence models.","order":3},{"id":"f15230c3-4ff7-4c86-9846-bedcb9792d00","title":"Transfer Learning, Fine-Tuning, and Model Adaptation","description":"Learn the practical art of leveraging pre-trained models. Strategically apply feature extraction and fine-tuning, master layer freezing/unfreezing protocols, and adapt models to new domains with limited data. Implement these workflows using PyTorch Hub and standard pre-trained backbones from `torchvision.models`.","order":4},{"id":"61719601-0668-47b2-b479-4bea938269dc","title":"The Transformer Architecture: From Attention to Modern LLMs","description":"Deconstruct the foundational Transformer block. Build the self-attention mechanism, multi-head attention, and positional encoding from scratch in PyTorch. Understand the encoder-decoder structure and explore its evolution into dominant modern architectures like encoder-only (BERT) and decoder-only (GPT) models.","order":5},{"id":"7a74754c-0ff0-4653-a5fe-d6b919175d1f","title":"Vision Transformers (ViTs) and Cross-Modal Architectures","description":"Extend the Transformer paradigm beyond sequences. Learn how Vision Transformers (ViTs) process images through patch embedding and the class token. Implement a ViT for image classification and explore the principles of cross-modal architectures that unify visual and linguistic data.","order":6},{"id":"7706380f-bc4e-4ed9-8a24-91abe0adaf0c","title":"Autoencoders and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) for Representation Learning","description":"Master unsupervised representation and probabilistic generation. Build standard autoencoders for tasks like dimensionality reduction and denoising. Then, delve into Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), implementing the reparameterization trick and the KL divergence loss to learn structured, continuous latent spaces.","order":7},{"id":"0e25fe88-9eaf-4f96-9ca0-00db04d8cd4a","title":"Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs): Framework, Training, and Evolution","description":"Understand the adversarial training framework for data generation. Implement the min-max game between Generator and Discriminator networks, tackle training challenges like mode collapse, and study foundational improvements such as DCGANs. Build a GAN to generate images and explore metrics for evaluating generative model performance.","order":8}]},{"id":"282f6191-46db-49e8-8859-51184e1c34cc","title":"Phase 8: Deployment, Scalability, and Specialized Applications","description":"This final phase focuses on moving models from research to production and tackling complex challenges. You will learn model deployment (e.g., with TorchScript), distributed training basics, performance optimization, and delve into specialized application domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, or reinforcement learning through substantial capstone projects.","order":8,"chapters":[{"id":"94ceb8a8-b8da-44fa-a685-e1870112ac6b","title":"Model Serialization, Formats, and TorchScript","description":"Learn to save and load trained PyTorch model states and architectures. Master TorchScript by tracing and scripting models, converting them to a portable, production-ready format that runs independently of Python, and understand the trade-offs of different export formats (e.g., ONNX).","order":1},{"id":"7d9bc5c2-c509-4a46-b2ec-c8193208a66b","title":"Model Serving, APIs, and Production Infrastructure","description":"Explore frameworks for deploying models as scalable services. Implement a model server using TorchServe or FastAPI, create prediction endpoints, manage model versioning and A/B testing, and integrate basic monitoring. Learn to containerize the serving application using Docker for consistent environments.","order":2},{"id":"c11aed5b-6f49-4acf-8a9f-9cb8a773d4fa","title":"Distributed Training: Data and Model Parallelism","description":"Scale the training process across multiple devices. Implement Data Parallelism with `nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel` for multi-GPU/multi-node training and explore Model Parallelism for large models. Understand core concepts like process groups, synchronization, and efficient gradient communication.","order":3},{"id":"7e653860-3b00-4dea-b24c-3819d136fe90","title":"Performance Optimization and Profiling","description":"Techniques to diagnose and improve model efficiency. Use PyTorch profilers to identify bottlenecks in computation and memory. Design Levels for Chapter: Building a Multi-Layer Perceptron with PyTorch's Full Toolkit
Description: This chapter scales up to construct a basic feedforward neural network using PyTorch's standard components. response:
Level 1: Conceptualizing the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)
Description: Define the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) as a stack of fully-connected (dense) layers. Learn its core architectural components: input dimension, hidden layers with widths, output dimension, and the role of non-linear activation functions placed between linear layers to enable complex function approximation.

Level 2: Constructing an MLP with `nn.Sequential`
Description: Build a simple MLP using PyTorch's `nn.Sequential` container for linear, declarative architecture definition. Practice stacking `nn.Linear` layers and `nn.ReLU` activation modules, and learn to print the model summary to inspect layer connectivity and parameter counts.

Level 3: Building Custom Modules by Subclassing `nn.Module`
Description: Move beyond `nn.Sequential` by constructing a flexible MLP class that subclasses `nn.Module`. Define the network layers in the `__init__` method and implement the computational forward pass in the `forward` method, learning to manage internal state and complex control flow.

Level 4: Incorporating and Experimenting with Activation Functions
Description: Explore the purpose and implementation of common activation functions within an MLP. Use PyTorch's built-in modules (`nn.ReLU`, `nn.Sigmoid`, `nn.Tanh`) and learn where to place them in the network. Experiment with different activations and observe their effect on the model's learning capacity and output range.

Level 5: Selecting and Applying Built-in Loss Functions
Description: Learn to quantify model error using PyTorch's `nn` loss functions. Select the appropriate loss criterion (e.g., `nn.MSELoss` for regression, `nn.CrossEntropyLoss` for classification) for a given task, instantiate it, and apply it to compute the scalar loss from model outputs and target labels.

Level 6: Configuring Optimization with `torch.optim`
Description: Automate gradient descent by configuring an optimizer from `torch.optim`. Learn to instantiate an optimizer (e.g., `optim.SGD`, `optim.Adam`), connect it to the model's parameters, and set hyperparameters like the learning rate. Understand the optimizer's role in applying the gradients computed during backpropagation.

Level 7: Integrating Components into a Complete Training Loop
Description: Assemble all components—model, loss function, and optimizer—into a working training loop. Implement the core iterative steps: zeroing gradients, forward pass, loss calculation, backward pass, and optimizer step. Execute this loop over multiple epochs to train the MLP on a simple dataset.

Level 8: Capstone Project - Training an MLP for a Standard Task
Description: Apply the full toolkit to solve a concrete problem, such as classifying the Iris dataset or approximating a non-linear function. Tasks include final model definition, data preparation into tensors, loop execution, and basic evaluation of the trained model's performance on test data.

Description: This final chapter integrates all skills into an end-to-end workflow. response:
1. Data Acquisition and Preparation: This level focuses on loading a dataset into Python, performing necessary preprocessing, and converting the data into PyTorch tensors. Learners will handle tasks like loading a CSV or using a built-in dataset (e.g., Iris from scikit-learn), separating features and labels, normalizing or standardizing features, and splitting the data into distinct training and test sets.

2. Model Definition Using `nn.Module`: This level covers the concrete implementation of a neural network model by subclassing `torch.nn.Module`. Learners will define the network architecture in the `__init__` method (e.g., linear layers) and implement the sequence of operations in the `forward` method, creating a reusable and callable model object.

3. Configuring the Training Components: This level involves selecting and instantiating the critical tools for the learning process. Learners will choose an appropriate loss function (e.g., `nn.CrossEntropyLoss` for classification) and an optimizer (e.g., `optim.SGD`), passing the model's parameters to the optimizer and setting hyperparameters like the learning rate.

4. Implementing the Training Loop: This level is the core of the pipeline, where learners write the iterative loop that trains the model. This includes stepping through epochs, performing the forward pass to get predictions, calculating the loss, calling `loss.backward()` to compute gradients, using `optimizer.step()` to update weights, and crucially, zeroing the gradients with `optimizer.zero_grad()` before each backward pass.

5. Model Evaluation on the Test Set: This level shifts to assessment mode. Learners will use the trained model to make predictions on the held-out test set. They will calculate evaluation metrics (like accuracy for classification) by comparing predictions to true labels, ensuring this is done within a `torch.no_grad()` context to prevent unnecessary gradient computations.

6. Analysis, Visualization, and Basic Debugging: This level focuses on interpreting the results and the training process. Learners will plot the training loss over epochs to check for convergence, analyze model performance (e.g., via a confusion matrix), and practice basic debugging by checking for issues like vanishing gradients or poor initialization.

7. Synthesizing the Workflow into a Reusable Template: This final level emphasizes abstraction and best practices. Learners will review the complete script, structure it into clear functions (e.g., `train_epoch`, `evaluate`), and document the standard pattern. The goal is to solidify this end-to-end pipeline as a personal template for future PyTorch projects.

Level 1: Conceptualizing the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)
Description: Define the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) as a stack of fully-connected (dense) layers. Learn its core architectural components: input dimension, hidden layers with widths, output dimension, and the critical role of non-linear activation functions placed between linear layers to enable complex function approximation. Reconcile this PyTorch representation with the foundational neural network theory from Phase 3.

Level 2: Constructing an MLP with `nn.Sequential`
Description: Build a simple MLP using PyTorch's `nn.Sequential` container for rapid, linear, and declarative architecture definition. Practice stacking `nn.Linear` layers and `nn.ReLU` activation modules. Learn to print the model summary to inspect layer connectivity, parameter counts, and understand the automatic parameter registration handled by `Sequential`.

Level 3: Building Flexible MLPs by Subclassing `nn.Module`
Description: Move beyond linear stacks by constructing a flexible, reusable MLP class that subclasses `nn.Module`. Define the network layers and operations in the `__init__` method and implement the computational forward pass in the `forward` method. Learn this pattern for managing internal state, enabling complex architectures, and integrating custom logic.

Level 4: Experimenting with Activation Functions in Practice
Description: Explore and implement common activation functions within an MLP using PyTorch's built-in modules (`nn.ReLU`, `nn.Sigmoid`, `nn.Tanh`, `nn.LeakyReLU`). Experiment with substituting different activations in a network to empirically observe their effect on training dynamics, model convergence, and output ranges.

Level 5: Selecting and Applying Built-in Loss Functions
Description: Learn to quantify model error using PyTorch's `nn` loss functions. Select the appropriate loss criterion (e.g., `nn.MSELoss` for regression, `nn.CrossEntropyLoss` for classification) for a given task, instantiate it, and apply it correctly to compute the scalar loss from model outputs and target labels.

Level 6: Configuring Optimization with `torch.optim`
Description: Automate and enhance the gradient descent process by configuring an optimizer from `torch.optim`. Learn to instantiate an optimizer (e.g., `optim.SGD`, `optim.Adam`), connect it to the model's trainable parameters, and set crucial hyperparameters like the learning rate. Understand the optimizer's role in applying the gradients computed during backpropagation.

Level 7: Integrating Components into a Complete Training Loop
Description: Assemble all core components—model, loss function, and optimizer—into a fundamental iterative training loop. Implement the sequence of steps: zeroing gradients, forward pass, loss calculation, backward pass, and optimizer step. Execute this loop over multiple epochs to train the MLP, observing the decrease in loss.

Level 8: Capstone Project - End-to-End MLP Training on a Standard Task
Description: Apply the full PyTorch toolkit to solve a concrete problem, such as classifying the Iris dataset. Tasks include final model definition, data preparation and conversion to tensors, execution of the full training and validation loop, and basic evaluation of the trained model's performance on a held-out test set. This integrates all chapter components into a standard workflow.

Level 1: Introduction to `nn.Module`: The Base Class for Neural Networks
Description: Understand the role and purpose of the `nn.Module` class as the foundational building block for all neural network components in PyTorch. Learn the essential template for creating a custom module, including the necessity of calling `super().__init__()` and the structure of the `__init__` and `forward` methods.

Level 2: Defining Layers and Implementing the Forward Pass
Description: Dive into the `__init__` method to define and store network layers (e.g., `nn.Linear`, `nn.Conv2d`) as class attributes. Then, implement the `forward` method to specify the exact computational graph by applying these layers and activation functions to the input data, using a simple Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) as a working example.

Level 3: Building Complex Architectures with Modular Sub-modules
Description: Learn to design sophisticated models by composing smaller, reusable modules. Create custom module classes for specific functional blocks (e.g., a ResidualBlock for ResNet), and then instantiate and connect these sub-modules within a larger parent network to promote code clarity, reusability, and maintainability.

Level 4: Parameter Management and the Module Ecosystem
Description: Explore how `nn.Module` automatically tracks all trainable parameters. Learn to access, inspect, and initialize these parameters using PyTorch's built-in initializers. Understand the model's state dictionary for saving and loading, and learn to register buffers for non-trainable persistent state.

Description: Master the process of feeding data to your models efficiently. response:
**Level 1: Understanding the Dataset and DataLoader Abstraction**
Grasp the core PyTorch abstraction for data handling. Learn the purpose and distinct responsibilities of the `Dataset` class (providing access to a single data sample and its label) and the `DataLoader` class (managing efficient batch generation, shuffling, and parallel loading). Understand why this separation is critical for building scalable, reusable training pipelines.

**Level 2: Utilizing Built-in Dataset Classes for Common Data Types**
Practice using PyTorch's convenient, ready-made Dataset classes. Learn to instantiate and use `TensorDataset` for in-memory tensor data and `torchvision.datasets.ImageFolder` for images organized in class-specific directories. Explore other common datasets from `torchvision.datasets` (e.g., MNIST, CIFAR10) to understand standard data loading patterns.

**Level 3: Implementing Custom Dataset Classes for Proprietary Data**
Master the creation of custom `Dataset` subclasses to handle unique or proprietary data formats (e.g., custom CSV files, non-standard image formats, or database records). Implement the two required methods: `__len__` to return the dataset size and `__getitem__` to load and return a single data sample (features and label) given an index.

**Level 4: Configuring the DataLoader for Optimal Performance**
Learn to configure the `DataLoader` to efficiently serve batches to the model. Explore key parameters: `batch_size`, `shuffle` (for training), `num_workers` (for parallel data loading), and `pin_memory` (for faster GPU transfer). Understand how these settings impact training speed and memory usage.

**Level 5: Applying Data Transformations and Preprocessing Pipelines**
Integrate data preprocessing and augmentation directly into the data pipeline. Learn to define composition of transforms using `torchvision.transforms.Compose` for image data and to implement custom transform functions for other data types. Apply these transforms within the `Dataset.__getitem__` method to ensure consistent, on-the-fly preprocessing during training.

**Level 6: Building an Integrated Data Pipeline for a Training Loop**
Assemble all components into a complete, production-ready data pipeline. Write code that connects a custom `Dataset`, a configured `DataLoader`, and a model training loop. Practice iterating over the `DataLoader` to receive batches, ensuring the data flows correctly from storage, through transforms, into the model for both training and validation phases.

overfitting/underfitting, and validation techniques provides the essential context for applying deep learning."},{"id":"36ded4f6-2844-4159-924b-8ea9b0875034","title":"Neural Networks Basics","description":"Conceptual familiarity with artificial neurons, activation functions (e.g., ReLU, Sigmoid), feedforward networks, the backpropagation algorithm, and core training components (loss functions, optimizers) is required before using a framework like PyTorch."}],"phases":[{"id":"a41118c1-baa3-465f-8757-84b2593e5386","title":"Phase 1: Foundational Mathematics and Scientific Python","description":"This phase establishes the critical mathematical and programming prerequisites. You will solidify your Python skills for numerical computing and learn the core linear algebra, calculus, and probability concepts that form the language of machine learning and neural networks, with no prior knowledge assumed.","order":1,"chapters":[{"id":"fcbf8c63-cbfd-4493-8b15-058428930624","title":"Python Programming Fundamentals for Scientific Computing","description":"Reinforces core Python syntax and constructs with a focus on numerical and data tasks. Covers essential data structures (lists, dictionaries, tuples), control flow, functions, and basic file I/O. Emphasizes writing clean, reproducible code and setting up a virtual environment for project management.","order":1},{"id":"9c6f9d31-b036-4e70-b014-826d92fdf7cb","title":"Numerical Computing and Array Operations with NumPy","description":"Introduces NumPy as the foundational library for efficient numerical computation. Covers creating, indexing, and manipulating multi-dimensional arrays (ndarrays), performing vectorized operations, understanding broadcasting rules, and applying essential mathematical and linear algebra functions.","order":2},{"id":"f1bf7e9b-c5dd-470e-9b06-3f95c6f5f86d","title":"Linear Algebra Concepts Applied with NumPy","description":"Presents core linear algebra principles through the lens of NumPy operations. Focuses on vectors, matrices, and tensors as data structures; key operations (dot products, matrix multiplication, transposition); and foundational concepts including norms, eigenvalues/vectors, and singular value decomposition (SVD) for practical application.","order":3},{"id":"b4ef56b2-afb8-4c03-af48-65cdcd4fef02","title":"Calculus Fundamentals: Derivatives, Gradients, and Optimization","description":"Introduces the differential calculus required to understand model training dynamics. Explores functions, derivatives, partial derivatives, and the gradient vector. Focuses on the conceptual interpretation of the derivative as an instantaneous rate of change and the gradient as pointing toward the steepest ascent, establishing the basis for gradient-based optimization.","order":4},{"id":"c1e18cf2-4a5b-4127-978a-7dc95e1c4609","title":"Probability Theory and Statistical Measures for Machine Learning","description":"Covers the probabilistic and statistical reasoning essential for ML. Includes fundamental probability rules, key discrete and continuous distributions (e.g., Bernoulli, Normal), descriptive statistics (mean, variance, covariance), and introduces maximum likelihood estimation and Bayes' Theorem at a conceptual level.","order":5},{"id":"8102a39d-5487-4eaa-acdf-118cc50ff477","title":"Data Wrangling and Manipulation with Pandas","description":"Introduces structured data manipulation using Pandas. Focuses on the core data structures (Series and DataFrame) for data ingestion, cleaning, filtering, grouping, and aggregation. Establishes Pandas as the primary tool for preparing tabular datasets for analysis and modeling.","order":6},{"id":"cd433acd-db08-4367-a941-dcceff261496","title":"Data Visualization and Exploration with Matplotlib & Seaborn","description":"Covers the principles of creating effective visualizations for data exploration. Uses Matplotlib to build foundational plots (line plots, scatter plots, histograms) and introduces Seaborn for more advanced statistical graphics. Teaches how to visualize distributions, relationships, and patterns to generate insights.","order":7},{"id":"b210a01c-a4b2-427a-bf5f-4516ebfa833d","title":"Integrated Capstone Project: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)","description":"A comprehensive project applying all phase skills. Students perform a complete EDA on a classic dataset (e.g., Iris, Boston Housing). Tasks include data loading and cleaning with Pandas, numerical analysis with NumPy, statistical summarization, and creating a visual narrative with Matplotlib/Seaborn to uncover key patterns, relationships, and hypotheses.","order":8}]},{"id":"5d2150c9-fee5-4868-bc9b-16aa00bf0c38","title":"Phase 2: Introduction to Machine Learning Concepts","description":"This phase introduces the fundamental paradigms and workflow of machine learning. You will learn core concepts like supervised vs. unsupervised learning, model training, validation, testing, overfitting, and basic algorithms (e.g., linear regression) to build intuition before diving into deep learning.","order":2,"chapters":[{"id":"7eedf760-778c-428b-b73c-a76d2e964ffe","title":"The Machine Learning Landscape","description":"This chapter introduces the core paradigms of machine learning. You will learn the definitions and key differences between supervised learning (for labeled prediction), unsupervised learning (for discovering hidden structure), and reinforcement learning (for sequential decision-making). The chapter establishes the fundamental concept of a model as a function learned from data, illustrated with real-world examples for each paradigm.","order":1},{"id":"f938a71e-63da-4a0d-a4aa-6af2f851bcc3","title":"The Model Development Workflow","description":"This chapter details the standardized, iterative process for building a machine learning model. You will learn the critical steps: problem formulation, data collection and preprocessing, splitting data into distinct training, validation, and test sets, model selection and training, and performance evaluation. This framework is essential for all subsequent practical work.","order":2},{"id":"6ae6a0d3-bb86-440c-a0c3-576bbe9985d4","title":"Evaluating Performance and Managing Generalization","description":"This chapter focuses on quantifying model success and diagnosing failure modes. You will learn key evaluation metrics for regression (Mean Squared Error, R-squared) and classification (accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score). It introduces the core concepts of overfitting (memorizing noise) vs. underfitting (missing patterns), the bias-variance tradeoff, and the role of the validation set in model selection.","order":3},{"id":"10fb70f1-263f-4a2f-b5e0-87100e7c0e8c","title":"A First Supervised Model: Linear Regression","description":"This chapter applies core concepts by building a foundational algorithm from first principles. You will learn linear regression as a parametric model, defining its hypothesis and cost function (Mean Squared Error). The chapter covers the analytical ordinary least squares solution and introduces the concept of iterative optimization, setting the stage for gradient descent.","order":4},{"id":"506cafa6-bd1f-47cd-9f45-b2cf071cb40f","title":"From Regression to Classification: Logistic Regression","description":"This chapter extends the principles of linear models to classification tasks. You will learn the logistic function (sigmoid) for modeling probabilities, formulate the cross-entropy loss function, and understand how to interpret model outputs as class likelihoods. This bridges the gap between linear regression and more complex classifiers.","order":5},{"id":"d9ac0fae-0b05-49b8-82f3-28b39d42e4c6","title":"Learning Without Labels: Core Unsupervised Methods","description":"This chapter explores the objectives and algorithms for learning from unlabeled data. You will be introduced to clustering (grouping similar data points, exemplified by K-Means) and dimensionality reduction (simplifying data while preserving structure, exemplified by Principal Component Analysis). The chapter contrasts these goals with the supervised framework.","order":6}]},{"id":"e9a313bb-0ea4-41f0-8d48-ad5b05a011fb","title":"Phase 3: Fundamentals of Neural Networks","description":"This phase demystifies the core mechanics of neural networks. You will learn about neurons, layers, activation functions, the forward pass, loss functions, and the essential backpropagation algorithm for training, building them from scratch using NumPy to deeply understand the concepts.","order":3,"chapters":[{"id":"9c88cba1-636e-4e04-b5fe-79b90de7fb0d","title":"The Biological Analogy and the Mathematical Model of a Neuron","description":"This chapter establishes the conceptual bridge from biology to computation. You will learn how the core concepts of a biological neuron (inputs, synaptic weights, summation, threshold firing) inspired the creation of the perceptron. You will then define the formal mathematical model of an artificial neuron, including weights, the bias term, and the weighted sum.","order":1},{"id":"856db600-2e92-4775-8557-40eefb67e157","title":"Introducing Non-Linearity: Activation Functions","description":"This chapter explains the critical component that allows neural networks to model complex patterns. You will learn why linear activation is insufficient and explore the purpose, mathematical form, and derivative of essential activation functions (Sigmoid, Tanh, and ReLU), comparing their behavior, output ranges, and impact on gradient flow.","order":2},{"id":"d966d901-ec17-4d65-a43d-378d5bcd6cdd","title":"Architecting a Network: Layers and Topology","description":"This chapter explains how to build a computational graph from individual neurons. You will learn to define a network's architecture through layers (input, hidden, output), width, and depth. You will understand how layers are connected via weight matrices and bias vectors, forming the structure for the forward pass.","order":3},{"id":"721eff62-ae5b-42c6-9a09-f74d023373da","title":"Computing Predictions: The Forward Pass","description":"This chapter details the step-by-step computation to generate a prediction. You will learn to express the forward pass for a multi-layer network as sequential linear transformations (matrix multiplications + bias addition) followed by non-linear activation. You will implement this full process in NumPy, calculating pre-activations (Z) and activations (A) for all layers.","order":4},{"id":"65deb479-73cf-4373-8265-c64d015b8453","title":"Measuring Performance: Loss Functions","description":"This chapter covers how to quantify the discrepancy between predictions and reality. You will learn the purpose and properties of loss functions. You will derive, implement, and apply foundational examples: Mean Squared Error (MSE) for regression and Cross-Entropy Loss for classification.","order":5},{"id":"b8c161e7-ae8b-4e8d-ab93-b49fe9c7d029","title":"The Engine of Learning: Gradient Descent & Backpropagation Intuition","description":"This chapter introduces the core optimization principle and the high-level logic of the training algorithm. You will learn the concept of gradients and how Gradient Descent uses them to minimize loss. You will then understand the goal of backpropagation—to compute the gradient for every parameter efficiently—and trace the flow of error backward through a network conceptually using the chain rule.","order":6},{"id":"ad1b70f3-d86f-428e-8194-4b19d0ba0a81","title":"Calculating Gradients: The Math of Backpropagation","description":"This chapter provides the detailed mathematical derivation for parameter updates. You will compute the gradients of the loss with respect to weights and biases for a simple multi-layer network. You will derive the formulas step-by-step using the chain rule for a specific architecture (e.g., MSE loss with Sigmoid activation) and translate these equations into a structured NumPy implementation.","order":7},{"id":"e96d91b5-49b7-4bfb-a3ce-0b069c01985e","title":"The Complete Training Loop: From Initialization to Update","description":"This chapter integrates all components into a functioning learning algorithm. You will learn methods for initializing network parameters (e.g., small random values). You will then write a full NumPy training loop that iteratively performs a forward pass, computes the loss, executes backpropagation to obtain gradients, and updates all parameters using a simple Gradient Descent update rule.","order":8},{"id":"67549fd3-8c51-4198-b68e-c3c7e6655e12","title":"Capstone: Training and Evaluating Your First Network","description":"This final chapter applies the complete framework to a concrete problem. You will generate or load a simple synthetic dataset (like the XOR problem). You will then train a small neural network from scratch using your code, monitor the loss during training, and finally evaluate the trained model's performance on held-out data, observing its learned decision boundaries.","order":9}]},{"id":"a91e37e4-99ad-4b1f-948b-e9af6b70efc4","title":"Phase 4: PyTorch Core: Tensors, Autograd, and Basic Models","description":"This phase is your first hands-on experience with PyTorch. You will learn its core data structure (Tensors), perform operations, and harness the automatic differentiation engine (Autograd) to efficiently compute gradients. You will then rebuild the basic neural networks from the previous phase using PyTorch's built-in components.","order":4,"chapters":[{"id":"372b180b-21a2-4c70-8976-76e34521d041","title":"Introduction to PyTorch and its Computational Philosophy","description":"This chapter introduces PyTorch, its ecosystem, and core philosophy. You will contrast its dynamic \"define-by-run\" approach with static graph frameworks, set up a PyTorch environment (including GPU verification), and explore the structure of the `torch` library and its seamless integration with Python and NumPy.","order":1},{"id":"9a30ddac-6f45-4d12-9d8a-9a90a9aaeea6","title":"The Tensor: PyTorch's Fundamental Data Structure","description":"This chapter covers the foundational Tensor object. You will learn to create tensors from various sources (lists, NumPy), inspect and manipulate their key properties (`shape`, `dtype`, `device`), and perform essential data manipulations like reshaping, slicing, and concatenation. You will also learn to move tensors between CPU and GPU memory.","order":2},{"id":"79c10c9d-f258-4d26-a8dc-e7baf9565981","title":"Tensor Operations, Broadcasting, and Initialization","description":"This chapter focuses on computations with tensors. You will perform element-wise and matrix operations, use reduction functions (e.g., `sum`, `mean`), and apply PyTorch's broadcasting rules for efficient code. You will also learn standard methods for initializing tensors (e.g., random, zeros), which are critical for setting model parameters.","order":3},{"id":"4b79099b-134d-458a-b1b8-e1323a6b68dd","title":"Automatic Differentiation with Autograd","description":"This chapter explains PyTorch's automatic differentiation engine. You will learn how tensors build a dynamic computational graph via `.requires_grad`, compute gradients with `.backward()`, and access derivatives via the `.grad` attribute. You will also learn to control gradient tracking using `torch.no_grad()` and `.detach()` for efficient evaluation and inference.","order":4},{"id":"4215b259-34c2-4218-a111-e9b51cfc8d33","title":"Neural Network Building Blocks: `nn.Module` and `nn.Parameter`","description":"This chapter introduces the high-level `torch.nn` API. You will learn to define custom network components by subclassing `nn.Module`, register trainable parameters with `nn.Parameter`, and use pre-defined layers like `nn.Linear`. The chapter covers the module lifecycle: initialization, the `forward()` method, and sub-module management.","order":5},{"id":"62685301-28ea-4dcb-9f4c-206156005082","title":"From Theory to Code: Implementing Linear Regression","description":"This chapter applies core concepts to rebuild linear regression. You will define a custom `LinearRegression` module, manually compute the mean squared error loss, write a training loop that uses `autograd` for gradients, and perform parameter updates with basic gradient descent, solidifying the link between theory and PyTorch implementation.","order":6},{"id":"ec769141-32cd-4b9a-a4c9-e843c58401b8","title":"Building a Multi-Layer Perceptron with PyTorch's Full Toolkit","description":"This chapter scales up to construct a basic feedforward neural network using PyTorch's standard components. You will build an MLP using `nn.Sequential` and custom modules, incorporate activation functions (`nn.ReLU`), use built-in loss functions (`nn.MSELoss`), and train the model using an optimizer from `torch.optim` (e.g., `optim.SGD`).","order":7},{"id":"22add941-997d-4925-8cb9-a1821c0084e4","title":"Capstone Project: A Complete Training Pipeline","description":"This final chapter integrates all skills into an end-to-end workflow. You will load a simple dataset (e.g., Iris), preprocess it into tensors, define a model, select a loss and optimizer, write a full training loop with gradient zeroing, and evaluate the final model on a test set, establishing the standard pattern for future PyTorch projects.","order":8}]},{"id":"3b14de34-b391-4745-8d4c-ada33a9cb02d","title":"Phase 5: Building and Training Deep Learning Pipelines in PyTorch","description":"This phase focuses on the practical workflow of building, training, and evaluating deep learning models. You will learn to structure projects using `nn.Module`, create custom datasets and dataloaders, write training loops, use optimizers and schedulers, and implement proper validation and testing protocols.","order":5,"chapters":[{"id":"08e24107-06d8-4b18-a0ca-9d892fff4135","title":"Architecting Models with `nn.Module`","description":"Learn to structure all neural network components using PyTorch's foundational `nn.Module` class. This chapter covers defining layers in `__init__`, implementing the `forward` pass, creating modular sub-modules for complex architectures, and understanding the model's parameter management. You'll build custom, reusable model classes from the ground up.","order":1},{"id":"12b9297d-2392-4eea-8659-9fe9c32ca473","title":"Data Pipeline Engineering: Datasets and DataLoaders","description":"Master the process of feeding data to your models efficiently. Learn to use built-in PyTorch Dataset classes (e.g., `TensorDataset`, `ImageFolder`) and, crucially, how to write custom `Dataset` classes for your own data. Integrate these with the `DataLoader` for automatic batching, shuffling, and parallel data loading, forming the essential input pipeline.","order":2},{"id":"0874ad78-8af0-4c30-a23c-7a927e0906a7","title":"The Core Training Loop: Forward Pass, Loss, and Backward Pass","description":"Construct the fundamental training iteration. You will learn to write the step-by-step loop that executes the model forward pass, calculates the loss using functions from the `nn` module, performs the backward pass via `loss.backward()` to compute gradients, and applies an optimizer step to update parameters. This chapter establishes the basic mechanics of model learning.","order":3},{"id":"286c96c3-1981-4887-a08d-80572823d83b","title":"Configuring Optimization: Optimizers and Learning Rate Schedulers","description":"Control how your model learns by configuring the optimization process. Select and instantiate optimizers (like SGD and Adam), setting their key hyperparameters. Learn to dynamically adjust the learning rate during training using schedulers (e.g., StepLR, ReduceLROnPlateau) to improve convergence and final model performance.","order":4},{"id":"8b5738c7-fb07-435b-87d9-535b09270d7c","title":"Implementing Validation, Testing, and Model Checkpointing","description":"Move beyond training to rigorously evaluate and save your models. Implement separate validation and test loops to monitor metrics like accuracy and loss, using them to detect overfitting and report final performance. Learn to save and load the complete state of your model and optimizer using checkpointing, enabling you to resume training and deploy the best model.","order":5},{"id":"ffcd8e6c-1c72-45fe-a704-ae719269a874","title":"Monitoring, Debugging, and Visualization","description":"Learn to instrument and diagnose your training pipeline. Implement logging for key metrics. Use tools like TensorBoard or Weights & Biases to visualize loss curves, model graphs, and histograms of weights/gradients. Apply practical debugging techniques to identify and fix common issues like vanishing gradients or poor initialization.","order":6}]},{"id":"63bee2c9-d1f4-428b-9173-953608cc7968","title":"Phase 6: Core Neural Network Architectures: CNNs and RNNs","description":"This phase explores the two foundational architectures for structured data. You will learn Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image data and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs) for sequence data, understanding their layers, design principles, and how to implement them in PyTorch for tasks like image classification and time-series prediction.","order":6,"chapters":[{"id":"a18031e3-5901-4477-a5ec-50eaa189ff87","title":"The Need for CNNs: From Fully-Connected to Spatial Hierarchies","description":"This chapter establishes why Convolutional Neural Networks are essential for image data. You will learn the limitations of dense networks for high-dimensional inputs, the concept of parameter sharing and spatial invariance, and the core idea of learning hierarchical features (edges, textures, objects) from pixels.","order":1},{"id":"17f8b475-b795-435f-b112-973bd439305b","title":"The Convolution Operation: Kernels, Strides, and Padding","description":"This chapter delves into the mathematical and practical details of the convolution operation. You will learn how filters (kernels) slide across input data to produce feature maps, and master the hyperparameters that control this process: kernel size, stride, and padding. You will implement 2D convolution from scratch in NumPy to solidify understanding.","order":2},{"id":"c19fa62e-e375-453b-b7aa-c34971ac1e87","title":"Core CNN Building Blocks: Convolution, Pooling, and Activation Layers","description":"This chapter introduces the standard layers that form a CNN. You will learn the purpose and implementation of convolutional layers, various pooling operations (Max, Average), and non-linear activation functions (ReLU) within the CNN context. The chapter concludes by stacking these blocks to form a simple, complete CNN architecture diagram.","order":3},{"id":"10612524-3f19-4a14-bf31-c38c765958e0","title":"Implementing Your First CNN in PyTorch with `torch.nn`","description":"This chapter is your hands-on introduction to building CNNs using PyTorch's `nn` module. You will learn to use `nn.Conv2d`, `nn.MaxPool2d`, and `nn.Sequential` to construct a network (like LeNet) for the MNIST dataset. You will define the forward pass and understand the shape transformations through each layer.","order":4},{"id":"91e34ca9-47cd-48cf-a879-c3271610611a","title":"CNN Application: Image Classification Project","description":"This chapter consolidates CNN knowledge through a practical project. You will build a more powerful CNN (e.g., a small VGG-style net) to classify images from the CIFAR-10 dataset. You will implement data loading, training, validation, and analysis of results, while exploring the impact of depth and filter sizes.","order":5},{"id":"4296efd9-e4af-4df4-a9d9-bf2b47607f62","title":"Introduction to Sequence Modeling and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)","description":"This chapter transitions to sequential data like time-series or text. You will learn the concept of maintaining a hidden state, the structure of a basic RNN cell, and the unrolled computational graph. The chapter covers the challenges of processing sequences of variable length and the idea of many-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many architectures.","order":6},{"id":"90d6a04a-b673-47b0-a552-0db9101d740e","title":"Advanced RNN Architectures: LSTMs and GRUs","description":"This chapter addresses the fundamental limitations of vanilla RNNs: the vanishing/exploding gradient problem. You will learn in detail the gated mechanisms of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) units (input, forget, output gates, cell state) and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs). You will understand how these gates enable the selective retention and forgetting of long-term information.","order":7},{"id":"38ba8e4b-c84b-4a62-aa9d-ff52d7474c10","title":"Implementing RNNs, LSTMs, and GRUs in PyTorch","description":"This chapter focuses on the practical implementation of sequence models in PyTorch. You will learn to use `nn.RNN`, `nn.LSTM`, and `nn.GRU` layers, manage input/output shapes for batches of sequences, and handle variable-length sequences using `torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence`. You will build a simple network for sentiment classification or next-character prediction.","order":8},{"id":"c0cf7431-8b31-44e4-b8ba-438aa081823e","title":"RNN Application: Time-Series Forecasting Project","description":"This chapter applies RNN knowledge to a classic sequence problem. You will build an LSTM model for time-series forecasting (e.g., predicting stock prices or weather data). You will learn to structure sequential data into windows, design appropriate many-to-one network architectures, and evaluate forecasting performance using metrics like Mean Squared Error.","order":9}]},{"id":"738f2bde-426c-4eb6-bc72-f8eb6ff7dce4","title":"Phase 7: Advanced Architectures and Modern Techniques","description":"This phase covers cutting-edge architectures and essential training techniques. You will study Transformer networks (the basis for LLMs), Autoencoders, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and learn advanced methods like transfer learning, regularization techniques, and hyperparameter tuning to build robust, state-of-the-art models.","order":7,"chapters":[{"id":"9489e5b2-8725-45ac-a9e6-82b2bca1b1fa","title":"Systematic Hyperparameter Tuning and Advanced Model Evaluation","description":"Establish a rigorous engineering framework for model development. Learn automated hyperparameter optimization strategies (grid search, random search, Bayesian optimization with Optuna) and implement robust evaluation protocols. Move beyond basic accuracy to detailed error analysis, confusion matrices, and specialized metrics for generative models (e.g., FID, Inception Score).","order":1},{"id":"128f7e2e-07f4-42b7-be5d-7f04f13e9a06","title":"Advanced Optimization Algorithms and Training Dynamics","description":"Master the modern optimizer toolkit. Implement and contrast advanced algorithms (AdamW, RMSProp, AdaGrad), apply adaptive learning rate schedules (cyclic, cosine annealing, warm restarts), and utilize techniques like gradient clipping. Diagnose complex training issues by exploring concepts of loss landscapes, sharp vs. flat minima, and the dynamics of vanishing/exploding gradients.","order":2},{"id":"deaf886b-dac1-4949-b82a-e5ac4f6b9d9c","title":"Modern Regularization and Normalization Techniques","description":"Enhance model generalization and stability with advanced techniques. Implement and compare normalization layers (Batch, Layer, Instance, Group Normalization) and study architectural regularization methods (Stochastic Depth, DropBlock, CutMix). Understand the theoretical motivation behind each technique and its application in vision and sequence models.","order":3},{"id":"f15230c3-4ff7-4c86-9846-bedcb9792d00","title":"Transfer Learning, Fine-Tuning, and Model Adaptation","description":"Learn the practical art of leveraging pre-trained models. Strategically apply feature extraction and fine-tuning, master layer freezing/unfreezing protocols, and adapt models to new domains with limited data. Implement these workflows using PyTorch Hub and standard pre-trained backbones from `torchvision.models`.","order":4},{"id":"61719601-0668-47b2-b479-4bea938269dc","title":"The Transformer Architecture: From Attention to Modern LLMs","description":"Deconstruct the foundational Transformer block. Build the self-attention mechanism, multi-head attention, and positional encoding from scratch in PyTorch. Understand the encoder-decoder structure and explore its evolution into dominant modern architectures like encoder-only (BERT) and decoder-only (GPT) models.","order":5},{"id":"7a74754c-0ff0-4653-a5fe-d6b919175d1f","title":"Vision Transformers (ViTs) and Cross-Modal Architectures","description":"Extend the Transformer paradigm beyond sequences. Learn how Vision Transformers (ViTs) process images through patch embedding and the class token. Implement a ViT for image classification and explore the principles of cross-modal architectures that unify visual and linguistic data.","order":6},{"id":"7706380f-bc4e-4ed9-8a24-91abe0adaf0c","title":"Autoencoders and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) for Representation Learning","description":"Master unsupervised representation and probabilistic generation. Build standard autoencoders for tasks like dimensionality reduction and denoising. Then, delve into Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), implementing the reparameterization trick and the KL divergence loss to learn structured, continuous latent spaces.","order":7},{"id":"0e25fe88-9eaf-4f96-9ca0-00db04d8cd4a","title":"Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs): Framework, Training, and Evolution","description":"Understand the adversarial training framework for data generation. Implement the min-max game between Generator and Discriminator networks, tackle training challenges like mode collapse, and study foundational improvements such as DCGANs. Build a GAN to generate images and explore metrics for evaluating generative model performance.","order":8}]},{"id":"282f6191-46db-49e8-8859-51184e1c34cc","title":"Phase 8: Deployment, Scalability, and Specialized Applications","description":"This final phase focuses on moving models from research to production and tackling complex challenges. You will learn model deployment (e.g., with TorchScript), distributed training basics, performance optimization, and delve into specialized application domains such as computer vision, natural language processing, or reinforcement learning through substantial capstone projects.","order":8,"chapters":[{"id":"94ceb8a8-b8da-44fa-a685-e1870112ac6b","title":"Model Serialization, Formats, and TorchScript","description":"Learn to save and load trained PyTorch model states and architectures. Master TorchScript by tracing and scripting models, converting them to a portable, production-ready format that runs independently of Python, and understand the trade-offs of different export formats (e.g., ONNX).","order":1},{"id":"7d9bc5c2-c509-4a46-b2ec-c8193208a66b","title":"Model Serving, APIs, and Production Infrastructure","description":"Explore frameworks for deploying models as scalable services. Implement a model server using TorchServe or FastAPI, create prediction endpoints, manage model versioning and A/B testing, and integrate basic monitoring. Learn to containerize the serving application using Docker for consistent environments.","order":2},{"id":"c11aed5b-6f49-4acf-8a9f-9cb8a773d4fa","title":"Distributed Training: Data and Model Parallelism","description":"Scale the training process across multiple devices. Implement Data Parallelism with `nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel` for multi-GPU/multi-node training and explore Model Parallelism for large models. Understand core concepts like process groups, synchronization, and efficient gradient communication.","order":3},{"id":"7e653860-3b00-4dea-b24c-3819d136fe90","title":"Performance Optimization and Profiling","description":"Techniques to diagnose and improve model efficiency. Level 1: Introduction to `nn.Module`: The Base Class for Neural Networks
Description: Understand that `nn.Module` is the foundational class from which all neural network components and architectures are built in PyTorch. Learn the mandatory template for creating a custom module: calling `super().__init__()` in the constructor, defining layers and parameters in `__init__`, and specifying the computational graph in the `forward` method.

Level 2: Defining Layers and Implementing the Forward Pass
Description: Practice constructing the network's architecture by defining and storing layers (e.g., `nn.Linear`, `nn.ReLU`) as attributes within the `__init__` method. Implement the `forward` method to define the step-by-step transformation of input data through these layers, using a simple Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) as a concrete, end-to-end example.

Level 3: Building Complex Architectures with Modular Sub-modules
Description: Learn to design sophisticated, hierarchical models by composing smaller, reusable `nn.Module` classes. Create custom modules for specific functional blocks (e.g., a `ResidualBlock`), then instantiate and connect these sub-modules within a larger parent network. This promotes code clarity, reusability, and simplifies the maintenance of complex architectures.

Level 4: Parameter Management and the Module Ecosystem
Description: Explore how `nn.Module` automatically tracks all registered parameters. Learn to access, inspect, and initialize these parameters using PyTorch's built-in initializers. Understand the model's state dictionary (`state_dict`) for saving, loading, and transferring models, and learn to register buffers for non-trainable, persistent state (e.g., running means).

Design Levels for Chapter: The Core Training Loop: Forward Pass, Loss, and Backward Pass
Description: Construct the fundamental training iteration. You will learn to write the step-by-step loop that executes the model forward pass, calculates the loss using functions from the `nn` module, performs the backward pass via `loss.backward()` to compute gradients, and applies an optimizer step to update parameters.
